title: Voice (sustained sung vowels)
reference_instrument: adult male voice, sustained vowels (VocalSet long tones, CC BY 4.0)
summary: A lumped two-mass vocal-fold model phonates into a 44-section MRI-derived vocal tract and the radiated pressure is read at a baffled microphone. The oscillation is not imposed: it emerges from the fold, the glottal flow, fold collision and the tract loop. The tract comes from one male speaker's MRI area functions in a speech posture (Story 2008). These are exploratory fixtures, graded against VocalSet singers on the three notes they sang (C3, C4 and F4), one pair per vowel and note. The fold law is now Ishizaka and Flanagan (1972) as printed, and every description was re-trimmed on it. 45 of the 48 reach their notes, which is by construction and so is not evidence; three do not, and one of those, story2008-u-C4, is graded, so it fails pitch. The pair files, and every graded count, harmonics-to-noise, attack and clock-ladder number on this card, were measured on the earlier law and have not been re-graded, and the vowel-ladder listening clip predates this law. On that law pitch, partial positions and inharmonicity were inside the real singers' spread on every graded pair, and the time-frequency picture, the spectral envelope, the attack time and the amount of natural fluctuation (the render is steadier than a sung vowel) were outside the real spread on most pairs.
physics_present: Two-mass fold of Ishizaka and Flanagan (1972) as printed, for both the glottal flow and the forces on the masses, with masses and stiffnesses from the licensed model-card pack and one stiffness factor per description: the entrance, Poiseuille, inertive, junction and exit terms of the flow, the printed section pressures on the masses, the closure force table, the nonlinear and collision springs, and the printed damping ratios (0.1 lower and 0.6 upper while open, 1.0 more while a mass's own section is shut). It self-oscillates against the tract as a port-Hamiltonian system whose stored energy closes (fs-couple glottis.rs, fs-phs). The ledger row ishizaka-flanagan-1972-two-mass-glottis carries the equations and the working readings.
A fold-tension gesture (`GlottalIsland::set_tension`, with the muscle's work reported so the stored-energy ledger closes).

Vocal tract as a 44-section area function from Story (2008) Table I, with viscothermal loss and a flanged-piston radiation load from the transfer-matrix duct (fs-duct), played through a convergence-laddered characteristic line.

Mouth volume flow from the SAME transfer-matrix duct (driving_point::outlet, a laddered FIR driven by the island's incident wave), radiated through the baffled circular-opening receiver at the paper's recording geometry: 0.30 m, 45 degrees off axis.
Output is the retarded derivative of the physical mouth flow at the microphone; the supraglottal pressure is never the output and no source waveform, formant filter or gain is applied.

Every render's provenance sidecar reports the passive closed-glottis formants of its own tract, mouth load and wall (passive_tract_formants_hz). The native transfer-matrix result agrees with Story's own calculation to a few percent (/a/ F1/F2 669 / 956 Hz against his 694 / 942 Hz; his measured speaker has 715 / 1180 Hz), so the rendered tract is the published area function, not an artifact of the solver.
physics_missing: Tract wall: the rigid-wall descriptions leave the first formant with a bandwidth far below the 50 to 90 Hz measured for humans. The -flanagan descriptions add the published yielding-wall setting of Flanagan et al. (B 1.6e4 Pa s/m, M 15 kg/m^2, via Birkholz, Haesner and Kuerbis, ICASSP 2022) for C3, C4 and F4 /a/ and /o/; /e/, /i/ and /u/ at F4 are not provided. The wall stiffness is UNKNOWN in that source (its authors neglect it; 1.48e6 Pa/m is assumed and a six-fold change moves nothing). The wall is a uniform lumped pin, not a measured distribution along the tract, and Story's own calculation, which included walls, puts F1 of /i/ and /u/ 64 and 72 Hz above our rigid-wall passive F1.

Convergence ladders: the bead needs at least three rungs on every declared axis. The mechanics clock (the fold's time step) now has one, on one case: for /a/ at C4 with an ideal-open mouth the non-harmonic floor of the render falls from the 48 kHz clock through 96 and 144 kHz to 192 kHz and is converged there (384 kHz agrees). Harmonics-to-noise by the grader's definition (tracked partials, at most 30, 80 to 10000 Hz) reads 22.4, 26.8, 31.8, 33.3 and 33.3 dB at 48, 96, 144, 192 and 384 kHz, against 39.1 dB for the real singers (largest real-against-real distance 6.6 dB); counting every harmonic to 10 kHz as harmonic it reads 22.5, 27.4, 34.4, 37.1 and 37.0 dB. An earlier version of this card said the render reached the singers' level and that harmonics-to-noise rose from 96 to 192 kHz in all nine real-mouth cases. Both were wrong as statements about the graded number: they compared a measure that counts every harmonic with the grader's, which counts every harmonic above the 30th as noise. Graded by P2 on the nine -flanagan-r4 slots, the change from 96 to 192 kHz is a mean of +0.6 dB, with two of nine down. The -flanagan-r4 descriptions use the 192 kHz clock because the fold contact is converged there, not because they grade better. These ladder figures were measured with the earlier Bernoulli-only flow law; they were not repeated with the viscous drop. Nothing else is laddered: the receiver's quadrature resolution, the tract line's tolerance and the fold's contact law.

Tract acoustics beyond one dimension: against the MEASURED volume-velocity transfer functions of the 3-D-printed Dresden Vocal Tract Dataset tracts (44 tracts, CC0, closed glottis, hard walls), the plane-wave transfer-matrix chain run on area functions that P1 derived from the same surfaces puts the first three resonances of the 32 vowel tracts, median model over measured minus 1, at -5.1, -3.9 and -2.4 percent with the flanged mouth and -2.6, +3.2 and +0.7 percent with a zero-end-correction open mouth, while DVTD's own 3-D finite-element calculation of the same geometry sits at +0.4, -0.6 and -0.4 percent. This tests the pipeline surface -> slicing area function -> chain, not the chain alone: the area-function method is not validated on a known shape (its volumes are 84 to 106 percent of the mesh volumes), the unflanged mouth load is refused for these mouths (ka 1.0), and the measured values lie between the two terminations for the second resonance. A resolved 3-D tract (fs-feec acoustics::helmholtz, beads pexfp.93 and .211) is being built as the like-for-like check; its result is not in yet.

High-frequency tail outside the receiver's resolved band: the render carries more power above 8 kHz than the real recordings, and it does not depend on the mechanics clock. The microphone's resolved band is 8 kHz (the last field of its line) and the one-dimensional tract is not valid above its first cross-mode cutoff, so these renders are valid below 8 kHz and the tail is not a prediction. The grader counts every harmonic above its 30th (from 7.85 kHz at C4, from 3.9 kHz at C3) as noise, so the graded harmonics-to-noise of our renders is set partly by this tail, not by the clock. One cause was found and fixed: the glottal flow had no viscous drop, so it fell linearly with the gap at closure, which gives the flow a corner and its derivative a step, and the harmonics fell at only 6 dB per octave (measured 5.5 to 7 dB per octave from 4 to 16 kHz, harmonic, the same at 96 and 192 kHz). The cited Poiseuille drop was added (glottis.rs e2dd8616d). Same descriptions, before against after, power in dB relative to the total at 8 to 10, 10 to 16 and 16 to 24 kHz: C3 /e/ -28.8, -27.5, -33.7 against -41.5, -41.4, -47.0; C3 /o/ -35.8, -31.9, -37.9 against -48.2, -46.9, -52.2; C4 /e/ -28.5, -25.6, -31.7 against -29.2, -30.6, -40.8; C4 /o/ -33.0, -29.2, -35.9 against -37.3, -36.1, -44.9; C4 /u/ -32.5, -29.6, -31.9 against -32.9, -32.0, -38.6. Real recordings at C4 for /e/, /o/ and /u/: 8 to 10 kHz -36.6, -42.7 and -57.4; 10 to 16 kHz -39.3, -43.3 and -49.5. So the viscous drop lowers the tail by 5 to 15 dB at C3 but by at most 4 dB at 8 to 10 kHz at C4 (and not at all for /i/), where /e/, /o/ and /u/ stay 5 to 25 dB above the recordings. This is consistent with the rounding lasting only as long as the gap takes to close through a fixed small aperture, whose duration shrinks as the closing speed rises with f0 (not measured separately). A prediction made before the render, from a prescribed gap waveform, said 43 to 50 dB at 8 to 10 kHz; it overshot by a wide margin because it took the gap waveform as given. Grader-style harmonics-to-noise (first 30 harmonics counted), before against after, at the re-trimmed pitch: C3 /a/ 21.5 to 25.9, /e/ 16.6 to 21.9, /i/ 13.7 to 22.2, /o/ 27.1 to 33.8, /u/ 26.5 to 32.3; C4 /a/ 26.6 to 24.7, /e/ 27.3 to 28.4, /i/ 28.7 to 28.2, /o/ 29.5 to 32.0, /u/ 31.8 to 32.1; F4 /a/ 31.6 to 27.6, /o/ 29.1 to 35.8. The graded values are P2's. The tail that remains at C4 is not explained (candidates: the forces on the masses, which keep the Steinecke-Herzel form, so closure is still abrupt in the fold dynamics; incomplete closure in real folds; tract losses at high frequency that the model does not carry).

Pitch trims on the printed law: every description was re-trimmed by moving its one stiffness factor with the subglottal pressure held, on the model alone, to within 3 cents of the note, and each card's header carries its trace. 45 of the 48 reach the note and hold it: from 1.5 to 2.8 s, past anything the trim saw, they stay within 2.66 cents. Three rigid-wall cards do not. story2008-u-C4 is graded and fails pitch: raising the factor alone it stalls at 226 to 232 Hz against C4 at 261.6 Hz, then falls silent, so it keeps its earlier factor and plays 210.5 Hz. Its -r1 twin does the same at 381.5 cents flat, and story2008-i-C4 stops at 250 to 252 Hz and plays 220.9 Hz. The note is 1.08 and 1.00 of the passive F1 of those tracts (242.0 and 260.8 Hz), and they stop at 0.93 to 0.97 of it. No rigid card reached more than 0.78 of its F1. No cause is named. All 48 share one recording level, full_scale_pa 8.0 Pa (112 dB SPL peak at the PCM ceiling): the loudest render, story2008-a-D4, peaks at 4.89 Pa and nothing clips.

Pitch grid and exact cycles: rendered periods sit on whole or simple fractions of the mechanics step (96 kHz on most descriptions, 192 kHz on -r4, 48 kHz on -r1), and rendered notes are exact cycles. On the 45 final renders that reach their notes, read at 16 bits on the 8.0 Pa quantizer over 1.5 to 2.8 s, every one repeats exactly; the period is a whole number of mechanics steps on 22, a fraction with denominator 2 to 6 on 16, and 7 to 15 on 7. Pitch moves in steps of up to about 4 cents against a smooth control, and those steps did not fall at 144 or 192 kHz on this grid: on /a/ at C4, over 33 stiffness values around the trim, the largest step read 3.93, 4.70 and 3.93 cents at 96, 144 and 192 kHz. gl_004's jitter of 0.0000 reflects that and says nothing about a voice's steadiness. The cause stays open on bead pexfp.325.2. The vibrato gate's extent half reads 41.0 cents for a = 0.08 against its floor of 41.5; a step on this grid reaches 3.93 cents, wider than that 0.5 cent miss, and that half is ignored with those numbers while its swing half stays live. A stepped vibrato contour has not been measured yet.

Singing posture: the graded descriptions use the speech configuration of Story's MRI subject, lying supine. Larynx height, pharynx and lip shape differ in singing. The only open sung-vowel tract tables found are the EBCT /a/ area functions of one trained male singer (Tom, Titze, Hoffman and Story 1999, NCVS report 14), and every sung condition there is FALSETTO; no open table of a modal sung tract was found. Entered with only the tract changed (bead pexfp.325.2), his spoken tract improves the C3 /a/ grade over Story's tract (the spectrum, harmonic levels and odd/even balance come inside the singers' spread, and nothing leaves), so tom1999-a-C3-speech-comf-flanagan is kept. The tract is better everywhere it was tried: on all five graded pairs (his spoken tract at C3, C4 and F4, his sung tract at C4 and F4) the spectrum, envelope and harmonic-level gaps fall. At C4 and F4 the count still drops by one measure, so those descriptions were not kept. At C4 harmonics-to-noise leaves: the renders are cleaner than the singers, because no aspiration or turbulence source is in the glottis (a stated gap of the source, not of the tract). At F4 the odd/even balance leaves, because F1 sits near the second harmonic. The falsetto tracts were driven by a modal two-mass fold, and the series tract has no piriform sinus, which in the authors' own model lowers F1.
Radiation: an infinite baffle replaces the head and torso, so there is no head diffraction. Nasal coupling, the piriform sinuses and other side cavities are not in the series plane-wave tract.

Tract and room gas: one gas fills the tract, the mouth load and the air at the microphone: saturated air at a declared 310.15 K (the physiological temperature is declared, not a cited measurement). The one cited breath state in the repository is a woodwind bore at 27 C and is not valid for the vocal tract. Swapping in its dry exhaled composition, saturated at 310.15 K, moves the formants by -1.1 percent (measured, not landed; it rides along with the next pitch re-trim). A separate room-air exterior would raise the radiated level by about 0.5 dB, a uniform gain that the grader level-matches away, so it is not built. Other declared gases reach the rendered sound. On story2008-a-C3 in CO2 the render's F1 to F4 move by 0.7834 against the c ratio 0.7706, inside the test's bound of 11.5 percent, the passive peaks move by 0.771 to 0.773, and f0 falls 3.5 percent. The amplitude centroid to 5 kHz reads 1.0552 of air, so it rises where scaling with c would lower it, and the share of its weight above 1.6 kHz goes from 4.7 to 12.0 percent. CO2's weight above 1.6 kHz is an open finding; the centroid assertion stays on record, ignored and failing.

Fold tissue: a lumped two-mass card, not layered body-cover tissue or a 3D fold. The damping ratios and the collision springs are the printed typical values of one model, not measurements of a voice. Pitch is set by one stiffness factor per description, found by iterating the emergent f0 of the model alone to the target note (within 3 cents, no recording involved), so f0 matches by construction and is not evidence of fidelity. The factor differs between vowels at the same note (1.12 to 1.42 of the pack values at D#3 on the rigid tracts) because the tract loads the fold; a physical fold-elongation law would replace this one free scale. The rest gap 3.57e-4 m is AUTHORED with no cited counterpart in the render path (glottis.rs, FoldCard::two_mass_standard); bead pexfp.194 names it as BR-04 #6, with the damping ratio the printed values have since replaced. The reproduction of the paper's typical row, gl_018, fails: it reads 167.25 Hz against the target of 150 Hz +- 10 percent, top of band 165, and is ignored with that number on bead pexfp.325.2. Measured human fold tissue is now in the repository (packs vocalfold-human-layers-kelleher-bmmb-pmc3745772, -elastic-set-alipour-jvoice-pmc3508138, -cover-shear-chan-rodriguez-jasa-pmc2561277, -indentation-layers-chhetri-jvoice-pmc2891297, all at 1 Hz except the cover rheology, geriatric donors): the cover shear loss factor G''/G' is 0.6 to 0.8 at 100 to 250 Hz (Chan and Rodriguez 2008, mean 0.74), a different quantity from a lumped-mass damping ratio, so nothing in the code uses it. The continuum fold with measured layered tissue (beads .26 then .28) is what replaces the authored numbers.

Subglottal system and player: the subglottal pressure is an authored player input, not a measured one: 900 Pa times the stiffness factor of the previous trim, held when this law moved the factor, so it is no longer 900 Pa times the factor on the card. There is no lung or trachea coupling. Vibrato exists as the card key `tension_modulation <rate_hz> <amplitude>`: a cricothyroid gesture that scales the three fold stiffnesses by 1 + a sin(2 pi r t). It is used by the sung C3 and C4 vowel phrases only, at 5.9 Hz with a = 0.082, derived from the mean rate and extent (about +-70 cents) of 50 professional singers (Larrouy-Maestri, Magis and Morsomme 2014). Measured on the rendered phrases on the earlier law, the pitch swings by about +-57 cents on average (41 to 68 by vowel), less than the 70 the amplitude was derived for. The graded notes are straight tones and carry none. Register changes and formant-tuning gestures are absent.

Regimes: on the earlier law the two-mass fold pair did not hold the target regime everywhere. At F4 the /a/, /e/ and /i/ pairs flip to a period-doubled oscillation (half the target frequency) within about 1% of the stiffness that gives the target, /i/ and /u/ found no usable F4 inside a sane stiffness range (/u/ only near 19 times the pack values), and /u/ at C4 oscillates irregularly (a broad comb of spectral lines, f0 spread 10.6 cents over four windows). F4 /a/ (+5.3 c) and /e/ (+9.6 c) are inside the bead's 10 cents but outside the 3 cents used elsewhere. C3, C4 and F4 exist because VocalSet's singers sang those notes. On the printed law, at the trimmed factors, the half-step partials of the 45 cards that reach their notes stay at or below -38 dB, so no period doubling is seen there.

Result of the wall on the largest graded gap, graded by P2 on the same slots: /u/ at C4 had an irregular oscillation (harmonics-to-noise far below every singer). Native probes showed it is not numerical (irregular at 48, 96 and 192 kHz mechanics clocks and for plus or minus one percent in stiffness; a rigid 96 kHz render stays irregular) and absent at C3 where f0 is far below the first formant. Adding the cited wall makes it regular and brings its harmonics-to-noise ratio and inharmonicity inside the singers' spread. Across all graded slots the wall is NOT a gain: the number of measures inside the real spread fell slightly. /u/ at C4 and /a/ at C4 moved outside on some other measures (the regular render sits further from the singers in spectrum and level pattern; the irregular one had matched some by accident), and several other one- or two-measure flips are at the edge of a wide ruler. The time-frequency picture and the spectral flux stay outside the real spread on most slots.

Natural fluctuation and onset: the graded references are straight tones whose f0 still wanders (SD 14-29 cents, measured on the references to describe the gap, never used as input) from neuromuscular irregularity. No open source calibrates that wander for trained singers (the one printed amplitude is a single singer's "1-2 Hz at 191 Hz", Titze 2014, and a 4-8x reading spread would make any value a knob), so our tones are steady and spectral flux is outside the real spread on 13 of 13 pairs. Calibrated amplitudes would come from Ternstrom and Friberg 1989 (STL-QPSR 30(3), not found open). The subglottal pressure rises over 150 ms, the centre of the 120 to 180 ms rise measured at the onset of a breath group in speech (Fant and Kruckenberg 2005: one male speaker reading prose, true subglottal pressure). That is a speech onset, not a singer's gesture, and no adduction trajectory is entered. The rise moves when the voice starts, not how it builds: the oscillation reaches 5 percent of its held amplitude at 128 to 149 ms (49 to 68 ms under the earlier authored 60 ms ramp), then grows from 5 to 90 percent in 10 to 48 ms (median 18.8 ms, 15.6 ms before), measured on the radiated pressure as a proxy for the glottal area. The glottal area of young non-singers at speech onset takes 88 to 116 ms (Petermann et al. 2016, the only open measurement found). Attack time stays outside the singers' spread on 10 of 14 pairs (ours 8 to 28 ms against their 22 to 580 ms). Two authored, uncited inputs set the build-up: the plateau pressure (900 Pa times the stiffness factor of the previous trim; about 3.4 times the fold's onset pressure at /a/ C4 on the earlier law), so the fold snaps to its limit cycle once past threshold; and the start from a seeded displacement of 10 percent of the rest gap. Neither is changed without a cited value.

/a/ at the converged clock: the flanged mouth load refused /a/ at 192 kHz (its mouth reaches ka 20.005 at that Nyquist against a bound of 20). The bound was a limit of the load's fixed quadrature design, not of the model it implements. Measured natively against the closed-form piston, the quadrature is accurate to 6.5e-14 across ka 20 to 26 and 2.9e-13 at 28, and loses its own 1e-12 gate at ka 30 (2.0e-11, then 3.6e-8 at 34 and 1.5e-5 at 38). The bound is now 24, tested at the cap and one unit above it. A 384 kHz clock for /a/ (ka 40) stays refused: the quadrature does not resolve it. /a/ at C3, C4 and F4 was then rendered at 192 kHz next to 96 kHz renders from the same binary. Harmonics-to-noise by the grader's definition (first 30 harmonics counted, which reproduces the graded value within 1 dB): C3 21.50 to 21.52 dB, C4 26.59 to 26.42, F4 31.57 to 36.66. So with the real flanged mouth and the wall, the largest remaining voice harmonics-to-noise gap (/a/ at C4: graded 26.4 dB against 39.1 for the singers, largest real-against-real distance 6.6 dB) is NOT a clock effect, and the ideal-open ladder above does not carry over to it. The 96 kHz /a/ descriptions therefore stay at C3 and C4. F4 /a/ gained 5 dB at 192 kHz, but its f0 moved to +4.6 cents of the note, outside the 3-cent trim, so it stays at 96 kHz until it is re-trimmed. What sets the C4 /a/ floor: the strongest non-harmonic lines are n times f0 shifted by constant offsets of 7.2, 13.0 and 22 Hz around every harmonic (for example 797, 1032, 1038 and 1058 Hz around the third and fourth harmonic, 48 to 55 dB below the strongest line in 80 to 10000 Hz), a slow two-frequency modulation of the oscillation. Scaling the fold stiffnesses and the subglottal pressure together by minus 3, minus 1.5, plus 1.5 and plus 3 percent gives 21.3, 27.0, 25.2 and 31.6 dB (f0 257.4, 259.5, 263.9 and 265.9 Hz) against 26.6 dB at the trimmed pitch, so neighbouring regimes do not close the gap either. The cause of the modulation is not established, and no fix was attempted: steering stiffness or pressure toward a regular regime would be fitting the measure. These /a/ figures are from the Bernoulli-only flow law. With the viscous drop and the re-trimmed pitch, C4 /a/ reads 24.7 dB by the same definition, and 32.8 dB at the unchanged stiffness, 5 cents flat: a swing of 8 dB from a 0.6 percent change in stiffness, which is how rugged that case is. /a/ at 192 kHz was not re-measured with the viscous drop.
